title: Sections of the comparison inverse image
statement:
Let $X$ be affine, let $F$ be an etale module sheaf, and write a basis object
as $U=\varprojlim_i U_i$ with $U_i/X$ affine etale of finite presentation.
Then naturally

$$
 (
u_X^*F)(U)=\Gamma(U_{\Et},F|_U)
             =\varinjlim_i F(U_i).
$$

The restriction $F|_U$ is the scheme inverse image. The same section formula
holds for sheaves of sets.

proof.text: Use the canonical comparison adjunction from [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For modules, the existing source-library theorem ProEtale.isColimit_comparisonUpperStar_mapCocone_of_isAffine gives continuity of the comparison inverse image on the specified affine etale presentation. Its unit is invertible on etale objects, by ProEtale.isIso_comparisonAdjunction_unit. Precompose its colimit cocone by the natural isomorphism obtained from this unit at the stages. IsColimit.precomposeHomEquiv then gives exactly the unit-and-restriction cocone proEtaleComparisonSectionsCocone, with no choice of section representatives.

For sets, specialize the coefficient-independent arguments of the source modules Comparison/FullyFaithful and Comparison/Continuity. A left Kan extension along the opposite etale-to-pro-etale inclusion preserves the filtered colimit attached to an affine etale presentation: the representable Hom functors preserve it by Scheme.preservesColimit_yoneda (finite presentation and affine transitions), and hence so does the left Kan extension. On the affine pro-etale basis [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], apply Presheaf.isSheaf_of_generates_of_isRelativelyPresentable to AffineProEt.minimalPrecoverage. The basis precoverage is finite and relatively presentable, its generating topology is the affine pro-etale topology, and filtered colimits in Type commute with finite limits. Thus this Kan extension of an etale sheaf is already a sheaf on that basis. Density shows that sheafification is invertible at affine pro-etale objects. The comparison unit is the Kan-extension unit followed by sheafification; full faithfulness of the etale inclusion makes the former invertible at every etale object. Consequently the comparison unit is invertible at every affine etale object. Transfer the Kan-extension colimit across sheafification at the limit and the stages, then precompose by the stage units as in step 1. These are the private, completely proved helpers setLanRelative, setLanSheaf, setIsColimitLan, setIsIsoToSheafify, setComparisonUnit, setComparisonUnit_isIso, setIsColimitComparison and setComparisonCocone_isColimit.

For either coefficient category, localize the pro-etale site at the weakly etale map U to X, using ProEtale.localizationRestriction and its adjunction to direct image. Evaluation at U identifies with evaluation of this localization at the terminal object over U. Direct images commute with comparison, via ProEtale.lowerStarCompComparisonLowerStarIso. Taking its left-adjoint mate with conjugateIsoEquiv identifies the localization of the comparison inverse image with the comparison inverse image of the scheme inverse image on U. Evaluate at the terminal object and invert the comparison unit there (for modules use the source full-faithfulness theorem, for sets the affine unit result of step 2). This constructs modulesSectionsIso and setsSectionsIso, naturally in F, between the exact two section functors in the statement.

Normalize the constructed isomorphisms against the required maps, rather than merely asserting an unspecified section isomorphism. Apply unit_conjugateEquiv_symm to the two composite adjunctions in step 3. Evaluate this identity at an etale object W and use naturality along the graph U to W times_X U. Its projection to W is the given morphism h, by pullback.lift_fst. Naturality of the comparison unit at the terminal object, followed by cancellation of that invertible unit, gives exactly modulesSectionsIso_leg or setsSectionsIso_leg: the comparison unit at W followed by restriction along h and the section isomorphism equals the scheme inverse-image unit followed by graph restriction. Apply this identity with W = D_i and h = pi_i, and combine with the colimit from step 1 or step 2. This proves both original existential statements, including every displayed cocone-leg equality. Empty affine objects cause no exception: the constructions use only the stated adjunctions, naturality and limit hypotheses, with no point or nonempty scheme chosen.
